name: Raising Spirits

angles.text: This task illustrates the restorative and spiritual purpose of modern orcish shamanism, using empowered relics to help heal lingering trauma among broken veterans.
Gor'mul embodies the deep spiritual malaise and dishonor felt by old veterans denied what they considered an honorable death alongside their past Warchief.
Under Thrall's leadership, the Horde actively seeks to reintegrate and uplift embittered veterans rather than abandon them to despair.

faq.answer: Gor'mul is an embittered orc veteran consumed by grief and survivor's guilt. Having survived the conflicts of the older Horde when his Warchief fell, he views living on as a cruel twist of fate and rejects conventional sympathy.

Tor'gan is a shaman trying to lift Gor'mul out of his bitter despair. Believing that reconnecting with the ancestral ways can restore broken spirits, Tor'gan crafts infused charms to remind former warriors of their people's spiritual rebirth.
faq.q: Who is Tor'gan and why is he helping Gor'mul?

aliases: why did gormul throw the amulet
faq.answer: The amulet was an enchanted talisman prepared by Tor'gan to reawaken Gor'mul's warrior spirit through shamanic energy. When presented to Gor'mul, he rejected it and threw it to the ground, feeling its magic was insufficient to dispel his deep bitterness.
faq.q: What was the purpose of the amulet?

faq.answer: While Gor'mul curses fate for denying him death alongside his Warchief in battle, he does not name him directly. His words reflect the tragic perspective of the old Horde's defeated remnants who longed for an honorable battlefield demise.

Tor'gan remains patient despite the initial failure. He acknowledges that the amulet was not potent enough on its own, but maintains faith that demonstrating the true power of shamanism will eventually rekindle Gor'mul's lost pride.
faq.q: What does Tor'gan plan to do after the amulet fails?

aliases: what does this show about shamans
faq.answer: The effort highlights the shaman's vital role within the new Horde as spiritual healers, working not merely to channel the elements for war, but to tend to the wounded minds and pride of their people.
faq.q: Why does Tor'gan use shamanism to help Gor'mul?

sections.body: In the wake of past wars, many orcish veterans struggle with the burdens of survival and perceived dishonor. Gor'mul is one such warrior, languishing in bitter despondency because he was denied what he considers an honorable death alongside his fallen Warchief. Tor'gan, an empathetic shaman, seeks to alleviate Gor'mul's suffering by reminding him of his people's spiritual strength. Believing that ancestral energies can heal emotional wounds, Tor'gan prepares an enchanted amulet intended to rekindle the old fighter's pride.
sections.title: A Broken Spirit

sections.body: When delivered to Gor'mul, the talisman fails to produce the desired effect. In an outburst of resentment, Gor'mul casts the amulet to the dirt, questioning why anyone would show him mercy when fate denied him an honorable end. Tor'gan takes the setback in stride, recognizing that a single charm possessed insufficient power to overcome years of entrenched sorrow. Even so, the shaman remains steadfast in his mission, resolute that the burgeoning practice of shamanism will ultimately guide Gor'mul back to his former honor.
sections.title: The Limits of the Amulet

summary: Raising Spirits is a Horde quest that addresses the lingering emotional trauma of an old orc veteran. Through the guidance of Tor'gan, a shaman attempts to reach the embittered Gor'mul using ancestral magic to restore his lost pride and will to live.
